title: Book 8 — Urania, Chapter 102
paragraphs: He thus consulted her, and she spoke these words: “O king, it is hard for me to succeed in saying the best thing when I am asked for counsel; yet, in the present situation, it seems best to me that you should withdraw and leave Mardonius here, if he wishes and undertakes this task, together with those whom he wishes to have. For on the one hand, if he subdues those whom he says he desires to subdue, and if the matters he has in mind when he speaks this way succeed well, the deed will after all be yours, master, since your slaves accomplished it. And on the other hand, if the opposite happens of what Mardonius intends, it will be no great misfortune, since you yourself will remain safe, and the power concerning your house in those parts will remain safe too: for if you remain safe with your house, the Greeks will have many contests, many times over, to pass through for their own existence. As for Mardonius, if he suffers any disaster, no account will be made of it; and even if the Greeks conquer, they gain a victory that is no victory, having destroyed only a slave of yours. You, meanwhile, will withdraw having done what you set out to do — that is, having delivered Athens to the fire.”
